# Cyrus build: what exists and what needs the owner (updated 2026-10-10)

Nothing below is deployed, merged to main, migrated in production, or switched on. All work is on branches, verified on node-2 / devhost.

## Branches and worktrees (chain; later branches contain earlier ones)
- `feature/cyrus-r0` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r0): version registry, launch-pair guard, starter-grant guard, reproducible jars, engine core (spec, revisions, namespaces, router, asset gate), Test Flight, pack delivery (pack host, managed plugins, Pack Loader), 26.x lane (inert), eval set (124 prompts).
- `feature/cyrus-r1` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r1): texture slice, sound slice (+ library manifest/taxonomy/search), texture library + unified catalog layer.
- `feature/cyrus-r2` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r2): r1 merged in + server inventory, conflict engine, Mod Packs. **The current integration branch.**
- `feature/cyrus-r3` (cyrus-r3): import-your-own-mod. DONE and merged into r2.
- `feature/cyrus-r4` (cyrus-r4): Data Pack Studio backend. DONE and merged into r2 (server.js/prompts.js conflicts resolved).
- `feature/cyrus-r5` (cyrus-r5): Studio UI part 1: shell, Texture Studio, locked states, library browser (in progress, from r2).
- `feature/cyrus-r6` (cyrus-r6): animated creature pipeline, BetterModel 3.5.0, 26.x first. DONE and merged into r2 (34 conflict blocks resolved; 1211 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r7` (cyrus-r7): gameplay designer engine (items + ability graph + 17-component library). DONE and merged into r2 (31 conflict blocks; 1325 Cyrus/builder tests pass; tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r8` (cyrus-r8): worldgen datapacks (custom dimensions/biomes/structures). DONE and merged into r2 (1394 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r9` (cyrus-r9): Sound Studio UI. DONE and merged into r2 (1468 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r10` (cyrus-r10): item model states + display contexts (bow pull, gun aim/reload, 8 contexts, studio In-game preview). DONE and merged into r2 (1429 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r11` (cyrus-r11): GUI menu + quest designers, extends the design kind. DONE and merged into r2 (1531 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r12`: integration/delivery (release record, Test Flight gate, delivery orchestrator with proven rollback, sound relay, admin read model). DONE, merged into r2 together with r13-foundation (1596 tests pass).
- Studio UI part 1 (r5: shell, Texture Studio, library browser, locked states) is DONE and merged into r2.
- Queued next: Sound Studio UI, item model states and display contexts, animated creature pipeline (26.x), gameplay designers, then R4/R5 of the master plan.

## Switches (all OFF; fail closed)
`cyrus_studio_public_enabled` + `cyrus_tok_live` (must move together; guard built), `cyrus_import_enabled`, `cyrus_studios_enabled`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`, `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1` (real plugin/pack install), `CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL=1`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1` (until set, customer builds get synth sounds only), `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` (render host), pack storage env (`CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE` + S3 settings).

## Needs your approval or action
1. **Production migrations** (additive, new tables only): `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-engine-core.sql` (4 tables + a trigger that must be run by hand), `2026-10-10-cyrus-managed-plugins.sql` (2 tables) then `scripts/cyrus-seed-managed-plugins.ts`. More may be added by in-progress agents (they report).
2. **VM 88001** (the deploy script /root/agent-notes/deploy-modbuilder.sh now copies every needed file incl. registry.json and deps.json; the Dockerfile COPY list was missing textures/sound modules before and is fixed and test-guarded): rebuild the build-service image with the new files (jar.js, textures.js, sound files, texture-example.json, datapack/import files when done), the JDK 25 build args, and make `registry.json` available inside the container; verify the hardened scan is live; check `/health` `auth` (API key vs subscription) and switch to an API key **before any public launch**; then one real build to confirm reproducible jars and the asset sections.
3. **Pack hosting**: choose storage provider/bucket (any S3 API; R2 has free egress), the public pack domain (`CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE`), retention for unused packs; deploy the Pack Loader jar to the worker host.
4. **Sound library**: confirm Excelerator.tech is yours, document the source per file group, then set `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`; write the customer-facing sound licence; review `sound-library-catalog.md`; set the render path (ssh key to node-2, worker only).
5. **Reviews**: texture contact sheets (`texture-library-sheets/`), the studio design mockups (`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/`), the 7 design defaults I chose (plan names Katara/Saka/Yakko, token cost shown on asset edits, packs optional with per-mod required option, 'Mob skin: coming soon', read-only mobile approve, full-page editors).
6. **Decisions**: should a Mod Pack with open warnings install without the user acknowledging them (today yes; I recommend requiring acknowledgement)? Import attestation wording and rate limits (when the import agent reports).
7. **Real-client test day** (someone with Minecraft): pack download and accept prompt, textures, item previews, sounds and subtitles, Bedrock note. Nothing resource-pack related is verified in a real client yet.
8. **Paid eval run**: approve a number of real builds and budget (the eval set is 124 prompts; a full multi-version run is 226 builds; ~30 texture prompts first); a baseline file is saved after the first run.
9. Delete when finished: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/r0-26x` (~2 GB) and old tmp dirs.

## Known limits (honest)
No real model build has been run for texture/sound/datapack/import sections, so the AI's output quality is unverified. No real client has loaded a pack. The vanilla-lookalike texture check is a stub. Test Flight runs one flight at a time with no container limits. 26.3 has no stable Paper build (only alpha/beta).

## Data pack studio decisions (agent report 2026-10-10)
Flags `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO` and `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL` are off. To go live: paid eval of model-written specs first, rebuild the service image (the Dockerfile list now includes the data pack modules), wire the delivery job (steps in docs). Decision: allow vanilla loot overrides? (out of v1). Known flaky test: test/cyrus-admin.test.ts fails only when run in the big parallel batch (passes alone, 31/31).

## Creature pipeline owner items (agent report 2026-10-10)
Flags: `CYRUS_CREATURES=1`, `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1`; mark a 26.x version buildable only after the image rebuild and an eval. Decide whether Nxeon pre-places BetterModel's libraries (it downloads 57 files on first start); place the BetterModel jar + seed the catalog; real-client test day (looks/animation unverified); the BetterModel pack hand-off must follow a server restart; suggested limit until a real-client test: 25 creatures per server, ~300 bones in one player's view. Template quality: ghoul and wolf good, the banshee reads correctly but its robe is blocky.

## Gameplay designer owner items (agent report 2026-10-10)
Flag `CYRUS_DESIGNER` is off. Decide: the pure 'just tweak a setting' parser `planDesignEdit` is exposed but NOT wired (skipping the model changes billing). Designer owns the main class/plugin.yml/config.yml; free-form Java only in `custom/`; every number/text/sound becomes an editable config setting; charged abilities = hold sneak then release. Not verified: any in-game behaviour (clicks, pulls, projectiles, recipes, loot), 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/26.1.2 javac (no classpath on node-2). Process note: each new asset kind touches the same 8 service/portal files, so agents must merge the latest feature/cyrus-r2 into their branch before finishing.

## Worldgen owner items (agent report 2026-10-10)
Flag `CYRUS_WORLDGEN=1` (also needs `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO`), off. IMPORTANT: a broken worldgen pack stops the whole server at its next start; the delivery job MUST roll back if the server does not come up after the restart, and that is NOT wired yet. Also decide: what happens to a dimension's world folder when its mod is uninstalled (currently kept); a small paid trial of model-written specs before enabling; image rebuild (Dockerfile updated). Limits: 2 dimensions, 16 biomes, 32+32 features, templates up to 48^3 / 32768 blocks, cost score cap 100. Performance: low cost runs on 2 GB+, medium needs 4 GB, high needs 8 GB plus pre-generation. Verified formats across 6 versions (1.21.2 carvers list, 1.21.4 music list, 1.21.5 dry foliage, 1.21.11 environment attributes + #rrggbb colours, 26.1 patch feature removed + dragon fight field, 26.2 lake rule fields).

## Item model states owner items (agent report 2026-10-10)
Flag `CYRUS_ITEM_STATES` off. Verified vanilla facts: bow = using_item condition then use_duration (scale 0.05, thresholds 0.65/0.9), byte-for-byte equal to vanilla bow.json on 1.21.4, 1.21.11 and 26.2; crossbow uses crossbow/pull 0.58/1.0 + charge_type (1.21.11 swapped outer layers vs 1.21.4); on_shelf context exists from 1.21.9; 26.x adds an optional `transformation` field we do not emit. Gun aim = a silent never-finishing consumable whose consume event is cancelled; held items refresh every 2 ticks; plugin 'mode' is one string (strings[0]) plus separate flags. NOT verified: how items look/switch in a real client; no javac on 1.21.4/1.21.8/26.1.2; the studio tab was renamed 'In hand' -> 'In game'. 1.21.1 legacy emitter is out of scope.

## Sound Studio UI owner items (agent report 2026-10-10)
Stays off behind `cyrus_studios_enabled`; library audition off until `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`. Decide: the library licence; whether committing the waveform OUTLINES (library-peaks.json, 64 levels per file, metadata not audio; not legal advice) is acceptable; sound candidates run as change builds on Saka (a new mod version each time); studio saves reach servers only on the next build; where production audio renders run (portal-to-node-2 render connection untested). Gaps vs mockup: narrower columns at 1440px (portal sidebar), header says 'mob' not 'zombie (silenced)', waveform legend below the box, cannot create a sound set from scratch in the studio. 23 sound-* screenshots in /root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/.

## Menu + quest designer owner items (2026-10-10)
Flag `CYRUS_DESIGNER` off. Caps: 8 menus, 16 quests, 6 slot rows, 10 pages, 8 actions/click, 8 steps x 3 objectives, 1-5 active quests/player, 2048 chars progress/player, one shared listener per mod. Real node-2 flights on 1.21.11 and 26.2 passed 21 RCON checks each. Not verified: any real client.

## Design v2 mockups (2026-10-10) - YOUR REVIEW NEEDED before any UI is built
/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v2/: item-designer.html, menu-quest.html, mod-packs.html, import-mod.html, datapack-studio.html (+ DESIGN-NOTES.md, 28 shots/). Questions: where production item icons come from (mockups use placeholder pixel art); should settings-only edits skip the model and cost 0 tokens; is the menu/quest scope right; may a pack install with open warnings; how third-party mods are added; is the worldgen restart automatic and are dimension folders kept on uninstall; is the simulator customer-facing; approve the import attestation wording.

## Multi-game 3D research (2026-10-10)
Sonnet research pass running -> /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/H-3d-games.md (go/no-go per game, where to start, foundation architecture).

## Foundation + community library (2026-10-10)
`feature/cyrus-r13-foundation` (worktree cyrus-r13, commit 6c91ab372b, NOT yet merged into r2): adapter asset-profile contract (Minecraft filled in, legal unreviewed), glTF sidecar manifest + legal-class ledger, worker-class job queue + content-addressed object store. 89 tests pass, tsc clean.
Owner idea 2026-10-10: every generated asset goes into a community library owned by Cyrus. DECIDED 2026-10-10: contribution is AUTOMATIC (no opt-in); ledger commit c94a65b061 (libraryEligible). Still needs before launch: ToS licence-grant wording (lawyer), content filters (trademark/real-weapon/NSFW), report/takedown. Excluded always: game-derived, third-party-licensed, imported-from-outside.

## R5 integration and delivery (`feature/cyrus-r12`, 2026-10-10)
No migration, enum or table. New OFF flags: `CYRUS_DELIVERY` (orchestrator master switch, worker), `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE` (boot-test sweep, worker), `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL` (block install/publish of a version whose flight FAILED). Sound render path: worker `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` + `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_PORT` + `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_TOKEN`; web `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=relay` + `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>` + same token (ssh is refused in the web process). Rebuild the build-service image (copies `release.js`). Before `CYRUS_DELIVERY=1`: an enqueue path for the `cyrusDelivery` GAME_MOD_SYNC payload, one supervised real delivery on an owner test server, and decisions on automatic restarts + the admin cleanup of kept dimension folders. Real node-2 results: `delivery-r5-flights-2026-10-10.json`, `testflight-gate-r5-2026-10-10.json`, `sound-relay-r5-2026-10-10.json`. Docs: "Cyrus integration and delivery (R5)".

## Model Studio design + plan (2026-10-10) - YOUR REVIEW NEEDED
/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v3-model-studio/: MODEL-STUDIO-PLAN.md (layers 1-4), 6 mockups (paint, cuboid/bone editor, car livery retexture, locked states, automatic library, AK-47 prompt flow), DESIGN-NOTES.md, 28 shots. Questions: plan placement (proposed: top "All models" plan); does "usable by anyone" in the library include "Use in project" (today's gate locks it); what happens to mods that use a removed library asset; real-weapon names (hold for review, not block); lawyer for ToS licence wording; budget for the paid AI-mesh quality test and a GPU worker; Hytale timing. Library eligibility gap closed in r2 (uploads, templates, derived content excluded). Blender headless proof of concept running -> I-blender-poc.md.
DECIDED 2026-10-10: Model Studio sits in the top "All models" plan (same tier as Texture Studio/Library). Server-side gate to follow when built.

## Host seam (2026-10-10)
`lib/cyrus/host` (settings, rate limit, audit, auth, access) merged into r2; `lib/cyrus/host/nxeon.ts` is the only bridge; `test/cyrus-host-seam.test.ts` blocks new Nxeon imports under lib/cyrus (baseline can only shrink). Behaviour inside Nxeon unchanged. Next adapters per L-separation-audit.md: db access (97 call sites), game install (GuestFs/engine), billing, worker entry. Decisions pending: Stripe model, SSO vs own accounts, domain, install API, DB/credentials.
## Hytale (N-hytale.md): conditional GO, adapter at maturity "planned". Blocker: each Hytale licence authenticates at most 100 servers; Nxeon would need the Game Server Provider entitlement. Official support pages 403; server/auth details from community sources.

## AI mesh / meshgen service (`feature/cyrus-r18-meshgen`, 2026-10-10)
Model Studio L4 as a flagged service: router (catalog -> template -> parts kit -> from-scratch script), cost estimate before running, node-2 sandboxed Blender worker on the job queue, checks, glb + manifest (`ai-generated-for-user`). All flags OFF, not wired into the build service, no migration. Report: `O-meshgen.md`; docs "Cyrus AI mesh (meshgen)".
1. **Pricing inputs (needed for any money figure):** set `cyrus_meshgen_price_input_per_mtok`, `..._output_per_mtok`, `..._cache_read_per_mtok` (USD per million tokens of the model you will use). Without them the UI can show tokens only. Then decide the customer price per asset: estimates are template ~5.7k tokens (measured 5.2-8k), kit ~11.6k (not measured), scratch ~19k (measured 15-20k), plus ~25 s of 4 CPU threads on node-2 per round, plus rejected rounds.
2. **Paid eval (budget decision):** 20+ real prompts per rung with a real model + vision look step, to measure success rate in <= 3 rounds and real tokens. Nothing here called a model.
3. **Isolated worker before rung 3 is ever on for customers:** the from-scratch rung runs model-written Python; the systemd sandbox held every PoC probe but a kernel escape is untested. Needs a microVM/gVisor worker (no network, no credentials). Rungs 1-2 run no model code and can use node-2 as is.
4. **GPU worker:** not needed for rungs 0-3 (Cycles CPU renders ~16-28 s). Only needed for faster previews (EEVEE) or image-to-3D (TRELLIS, MIT) later.
5. **Game budgets:** no shipped game declares `AssetProfile.meshBudget`; every real game is refused until its adapter sets one (FiveM/UE numbers need a person to check the engine docs). The flights used a made-up draft profile.
6. **Template roadmap (proposal):** next pistol/shotgun (rifle kit reuse), barrel/drum + lantern (kit already does them), furniture (table/chair/shelf), sci-fi panel/terminal, melee axe/hammer/mace (the sword excludes these words today), vehicle parts much later. Known weak: the rifle `drum` magazine reads like a wheel; the wooden crate's bands are thin.
7. Switch on order when ready: `CYRUS_MESHGEN=1` on the worker host only after the build-service wiring, the plan gate (Model Studio = "All models") and the catalog registration exist; `CYRUS_MESHGEN_SCRATCH=1` only after item 3.

## Catalog v2 (`feature/cyrus-r14-catalog`, 2026-10-10)
Metadata + tagging + retrieval layer (`lib/cyrus/library/v2`): CatalogEntry v1 (situations, quality score, per-game fit, licence tier), zero-token stage A, stage-B planner/estimator with a hard budget (no model called), stage-C review data, content filters, catalog_search/catalog_get tools. Report: `M-catalog-v2.md`; docs "Cyrus asset catalog (v2)". Measured: stage A fully describes 54.7 % of the staged CC0 catalog (models 98.7 %, sprites 41.6 %), 76.9 % of SFX names. Tagging 100k assets is ~$12 / $24 / $47 at cheap/mid/top list prices (prices are inputs; verify).
1. Migration `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-catalog-v2.sql` (3 new tables, additive, NOT applied).
2. Decide licence tiers per plan (`PLAN_TIERS` in `lib/cyrus/library/v2/tools.ts`).
3. Clear the proprietary SFX library per pack (licence text per folder) before customer builds; decide on real-gun pack names (flagged today).
4. Stage-B approval: tier + token cap per run (ledger table `CyrusCatalogEnrichmentRun`); suggested first step a 500-asset cheap-tier run on sprites.
5. Extend the trademark stub list; confirm "hold for owner review" for community assets named after real guns.
6. Asset-profile catalog hints for each next game (only Minecraft has them).

## Model Studio Layer 1: viewport + paint (`feature/cyrus-r16-viewport`, 2026-10-10)
Built behind flags, NOT deployed, NOT merged into a release. Docs: "Cyrus Model Studio: viewport and paint". Screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/modelstudio-*.png`. The UI follows the v3 paint mockup, which you have NOT reviewed yet: please review the mockup and these shots together.
1. **Two settings, both off:** `cyrus_studios_enabled` (existing) AND the new `cyrus_model_studio_enabled`. Until both are on, only preview accounts see /studio/model. The new key is not in the admin settings catalog yet (add it there when you want a toggle in /admin).
2. **One new table** `CyrusModelDraft` (autosave drafts; no FKs). Needs the normal schema push at deploy, before the flag. Without it autosave answers "not available" (no 500s) and saving revisions still works.
3. **Plan gate as you decided:** paint/fill/decal/layers/drafts/save = "All models" only, server side, unknown plan = closed; view/orbit/previews/install/export never gated. Lower plans get the page in view-only.
4. **Finding to decide (guns):** the new grip_in_hand check shows today's Cyrus handgun defaults put the grip ~2/16 block from where vanilla holds tools in third person (3/16 in first person, 5/16 for the template's aiming state). Cause: the re-grip is computed under the gun's own rotation. Options: (a) re-grip to the vanilla fist (my recommendation, a small change in `lib/cyrus/textures/display.ts`, it changes shipped packs), (b) keep and verify on the real-client day. Either way: one Test Flight with a real client holding the pistol.
5. **Not built yet (next tasks):** compiling painted creature skins into the delivered BetterModel model (creature paint is saved as revisions only; item paint DOES ship, through the Texture Studio save); the production transport for the server preview renderer (it runs Chromium, so only on node-2; `CYRUS_MODEL_PREVIEW=local` is refused in production); AI model candidates (the prompt dock is shown disabled); an entry link from the mod's Assets tab; ItemCuboidSpec 3D items (plan F3).
6. **Decisions taken here (change if you disagree):** half-transparent paint on items is snapped to solid/clear (Minecraft cutout); "Fill" defaults to the whole face (Same colour is an option); mirror reflects across the model's centre plane; layers per model max 16; a dev-only sample glTF crate appears in the model list only off production.

# Cyrus Master Plan: the ultimate game-mod creation studio (Minecraft first)

Date: 2026-10-10. Owner direction: build the ultimate mod creation studio; launch is months away; other concerns later. Sources: the four owner documents (Master Update Plan, Texture & Sound plan, Minecraft Feature Roadmap, multi-game prompt), research files E, G, A, A2, B, C, D, F, and the red-team review GAPS-AND-IDEAS.md, all in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/`. Research claims are labelled VERIFIED or UNVERIFIED in those files; this plan inherits their labels and adds none of its own. Sizes are S/M/L effort.

## 1. What we are building
A real game-mod **engine**, not a prompt box. The source of truth is a typed, versioned **mod project**; the AI is the author and editor inside it; deterministic generators, validators and a real-server test harness turn the project into artifacts; studios and designers edit the same project; mods compose into Mod Packs; users can bring their own mods. Minecraft is adapter #1 on a game-agnostic core.

**Principles**
1. Engine first: every feature must be typed, validated, testable, editable and composable. A prompt wrapper is not a feature.
2. Evidence over claims: no status ("built", "tested", "supported") that did not actually run. Compile, scan, boot test and functional test are separate checks.
3. Foundation for other games: shared core behind interfaces; per-game adapters (Section 4.10).
4. Honest about limits: the router tells users what a vanilla client can and cannot do.
5. Dependencies decide order, not enthusiasm (the review found five dependency inversions in the first schedule; this plan fixes them).

## 2. Decisions already made by the owner
- Plan tiers: Free and Katara get no studios; **Saka gets Sound Studio + Sound Library; the top plan (`all`, includes Yakko) gets everything** including Texture Studio + Texture Library. Tiers are cumulative.

### 4.6 Test Flight (M, lite first)
Disposable Paper server per target version on node-2 (MEASURED 2026-10-10 with Test Flight lite: 26.x 10.4-10.8 s boot, 722-803 MB peak RSS; 1.21.11 on JDK 21 18.0 s, 878 MB; whole flight 12-20 s; see docs "Cyrus Test Flight (R0)"): boot, plugin enabled, RCON commands, `datapack list`, log matcher, clean shutdown. Later: MockBukkit logic tests, Mineflayer scenario bots (MIT, supports through 26.1), performance scenarios. Honest per-check status table; no "success" if a required stage was skipped. Concurrency capped (a past node crash came from parallel builds).

### 4.7 Asset pipeline and studios
Shared studio core + per-game profile. Minecraft = pixel profile.
- **Texture** (top plan): LLM writes a pixel spec (palette + shapes), deterministic renderer draws it (raise the 400-op / 16-64 px limits for skins and larger atlases), optional pixel-model candidates later; per-mod **Style DNA** (palette ramps, outline rule, noise) for consistency; per-version validation; AI edits arrive as non-destructive candidates.
- **Sound** (Saka+): `SoundSpec` (events -> layers -> processing); tag the 514-file library by filename category; synthesis presets; processing in the browser from WAV, **server-side ffmpeg/libvorbis to mono Ogg Vorbis**; new namespaced sound keys played by the plugin (and silence the vanilla base mob; never override vanilla keys globally); mandatory subtitle keys. A complete mob set: ambient, hurt, death, step, attack, ability, spawn.
- **Models** (26.x first): `RigSpec` compiled by Nxeon code (3 archetypes, 5 procedural clips) to .bbmodel for **BetterModel** (MIT, pinned managed plugin). Handgun and similar items use static item models with display transforms, sounds and particles, no engine. Do not embed Blockbench (GPL app); do not depend on ModelEngine/FreeMinecraftModels/CraftEngine.
- **Quality bar**: rubric + metrics (texture palette size, contrast, edge density, banding, transparent policy; sound mono, true peak, loudness band per role, silence ratio) plus a vision-model judge calibrated on 100 owner-labelled samples; owner reviews a gallery.
- **Studios**: v1 minimal (miniPaint MIT stopgap or a small pixel editor; wavesurfer.js BSD waveform with trim/fade/layer and JSON edit recipes), then the full editors in R3. Library browsing follows the studio gate.

### 4.8 Conflict engine and Mod Packs (L)
- **Server inventory** first: read-only scan of jars' descriptors, `server.properties`, datapacks, existing pack owners. This is the conflict engine's input (and the "Server Doctor" feature below).
- **Static classes**: plugin names, commands/aliases (incl. Brigadier root literals and vanilla overrides), permissions, depend/softdepend/loadbefore DAG, api-version/Java/Folia, registered events + priorities, NamespacedKey/PDC keys, legacy `custom_model_data` integers and `item_model` keys, recipe keys, sound event keys, single-owner resources (Vault economy/permission provider, chat renderer, tab list, sidebar, world rules), datapack `replace:true` tags and double-overridden vanilla ids, resource-pack whole-file overrides, `sounds.json`/atlas/lang merges, font codepoint overlap, unmergeable shaders, budget classes (display entities, tasks, pack size).
- **Resolution**: reserved namespaces prevent most clashes; command alias rewrites; priority ordering; Pack Loader stacking; evaluate Weld/Beet (MIT) as an offline merge subprocess behind golden tests. Severity report: blocking / warn / info.
- **Dynamic**: one combined boot and one differential boot per changed mod; pairwise only for statically flagged pairs.
- **Mod Pack**: an Nxeon manifest shaped like mrpack (files with path/sha1/sha512/downloads/env, override dirs, platform=paper). Third-party jars by URL + hash, only Cyrus-built artifacts embedded. Versioned, changelog, compatibility matrix, combined test report; installs and rolls back as one unit; never contains Paper/vanilla jars. Not gated by plan.

### 4.9 Import your own mod (L)
Source-only first: copy `src/main/java|resources`, drop and ignore the uploader's build files (their build is never run), compile with the service template and a **curated checksum-pinned dependency allowlist** (also the basis for first-class integrations: Vault, LuckPerms, PlaceholderAPI as soft bridge). Unsupported: Kotlin, Lombok, annotation processors. Ingestion limits (zip-slip, zip bomb ratio, nested jars, multi-release, class major), no execution at ingestion, ownership attestation record, detected licence, public sharing only with consent. Two scan profiles: strict for generated, **attested/imported** with warnings and no "safe" claim. Imported source becomes revision 0 and uses the same change planner, tests, versions and install path. Jar-only imports are analysis and diagnosis only (decompile for navigation, never into shared knowledge). Not gated by plan; model use and assets follow tokens and the asset gates.

### 4.10 Per-game adapter contract (S, define in R0)
Artifact types and routes; toolchain profile and deny-list scan; version registry; knowledge pack; asset formats and **delivery** (Minecraft: server-pushed pack; Valheim: client zip; Terraria/Palworld: none; tModLoader: client mod); install rules; test lane; maturity level. Add `game` to every id and registry. Texture/Sound studios light up only where the adapter declares an asset format and delivery path. A realistic 3D/PBR profile is a later track; build only the interfaces now.

### 4.11 Data packs (M)
Typed spec -> per-version emitters (the AI never hand-writes JSON); schema source vanilla-mcdoc (MIT); static validation then boot a real headless Paper and test over RCON. MVP: recipes, loot, advancements, tags, functions, enchantments. Worldgen (biomes, structures, dimensions) later; `/reload` does not reload worldgen, so those changes need a restart.

## 5. Roadmap (ordered by dependency)
Calendar note: the review estimated R0-R2 at about 5-7 weeks including owner waits (UNVERIFIED judgement). The owner has beaten estimates; treat these as sequencing and relative size, not promises. (T) = real Minecraft client needed, (O) = owner action.

content.content:
## Cyrus Test Flight (R0)

"Test Flight lite" (2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r0`, **not wired into the build path, nothing deployed**): boot ONE throwaway real Paper server for one registry version on node-2, load the given plugin jars / datapacks, run the checks, tear it down, return a JSON report. Master plan 4.6.

**Files**
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/runner.js`: the runner (plain Node, no deps; runs on node-2 as root). `node runner.js run <resolved-spec.json>` prints the report JSON; `node runner.js setup 21|25` fetches + verifies a pinned JDK.
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/lib.js`: its pure helpers (log matchers + default ignores, plugin.yml-from-jar reader, `plugins` reply parser, RCON wire format, server.properties, resolved-spec validation).
- `services/modbuilder/tools/testflight/fixtures/`: `hello` (positive control, `/tfhello`), `broken` (throws in onEnable), `datapack-tf_smoke` (one function), `build.sh` (javac `--release N -proc:none` against a classpath file + reproducible `jar --date`, same as the build service).
- `lib/cyrus/testflight/types.ts` (spec/report types), `spec.ts` (`validateSpec`, `resolveSpec`, `requiredStages`; fail closed on the registry), `summary.ts` (`summarize`, `mergeSummaries`, `describe`), `client.ts` (`runTestFlight`, `sshRemote`, injectable `Remote`).
- Spec extras (added with pack delivery): `files` (small text files placed under `plugins/` before boot, max 16 x 64 KB) and per-RCON-check `writeFile` / `waitMs` (replace a file, optionally wait up to 30 s, then send the command), so a plugin's config reload can be tested. Both validators (`spec.ts`, `lib.js`) confine paths to `plugins/<plain segments>`.
- Tests: `test/cyrus-testflight.test.ts` (pure, 24 tests), `test/cyrus-testflight-real.ts` (real node-2 runs, run by hand: `tsx test/cyrus-testflight-real.ts all --out r.json`).
- Registry: `paperBuild`/`paperServerSha256` now also pin the **server** jar for 1.21.11 (build 132, Fill STABLE). A version without a server pin cannot be test-flown (1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8 and 26.3 today).

**Checks, in order** (each `pass` / `fail` / `not_run` with evidence lines; a check never passes unless it ran):
1. `boot_done`: a `Done (Xs)!` line within `bootSec` (default 180).
2. `plugins_enabled`: per plugin (name read from the jar's plugin.yml / paper-plugin.yml): log has `Enabling <name> v`, no `Error occurred while enabling`, no `Disabling <name>` before stop, and the RCON `plugins` listing shows it green (red = disabled = fail).
3. `startup_log_clean`: default matchers (ERROR/FATAL level, exception headers, enable/load errors, datapack load errors) over the log up to the Done line. Spec `logMatchers` replace them (an empty list is refused), `logIgnore` adds ignores. The two built-in ignores cover only noise the sandbox itself causes (no internet: Mojang public-key fetch, Paper version fetch); ignored lines are counted in the evidence.
4. `rcon_checks`: spec commands with `expect`/`expectNot` substrings (colour codes stripped), plus an automatic `datapack list enabled` check per datapack. stop/restart/op/deop/reload are reserved.
5. `clean_stop`: `stop` over RCON (stdin fallback), exit code 0 within `stopSec`, no matcher hits during shutdown.
6. `no_leaks`: our java PID gone, no process anywhere carrying this run's `-Dnxeon.testflight.run=<runId>` marker, no listening port in the reserved range (checked inside the netns and on the host).

## Cyrus integration and delivery (R5)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r12` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN 4.4 (engine release id), 4.5, 4.6, 4.8, R0/R2 and "Engine layers" 9 (delivery + lifecycle). **Nothing is deployed or switched on; no migration, no new table, no new enum value.** Everything new is behind OFF flags: `CYRUS_DELIVERY` (master switch of the orchestrator), `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE`, `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL`, and the sound relay env; each delivery part stays behind its existing flag (`CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL` (+ `CYRUS_WORLDGEN`), `CYRUS_CREATURES`, `CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL`). With all of them unset the only behaviour change is that a succeeded build gets an `engineRelease` key in its `ModBuild.cyrus` JSON (bookkeeping, stripped from customer views).

**Host seam.** `lib/cyrus/delivery/*` and the gate never import Nxeon internals beyond what Cyrus already used (`mods/guest-fs` types, `db` in the existing `*-worker.ts` pattern, lazily). Nxeon implements the small interfaces in the worker: `worker/cyrus-delivery.ts` (server file access through `SshGuestFs`/`LocalGuestFs`, the Mods-engine Cyrus installer, restart through the existing `powerScript`, RCON through `runRcon`, managed-plugin refs through `lib/cyrus/managed/service.ts`, pack hosting through `selectPackStore`). No new logins, plans or tables: Cyrus stays inside Nxeon and can stand alone later by re-implementing `DeliveryHost`.

### 1. Engine release record (`lib/cyrus/engine-core/release.ts`, `services/modbuilder/release.js`)
"Prove what built every mod." The build service attaches `release` to every succeeded build record (and a service summary on `/health`): base prompt version + per-section prompt versions (assets, datapack(+worldgen), design, itemmodel), knowledge version, API sheet name + sha256, rules version + sha256, scanner (`scan.js`) sha256 + scan profile (strict / attested), registry file sha256, JDK release + version (read from the JDK's `release` file, javac is never run for it), classpath file sha256, the allowlisted compile-only dependencies used (id + sha256 = SBOM-lite), toolchain line, image version. Anything it cannot read is `null`, never guessed.
`buildEngineRelease()` (pure) merges that with what the portal knows (the jar sha256 it re-hashed after download, its own registry hash, `/health` cached 5 min as a fallback for older images) into `{ schema: 1, id: "er1-<20 hex>", recordedAt, target, prompts, knowledge, sheets, rules, scanner, service, registry { portal, service, match }, jdk, artifact { kind: jar, name, sha256 }, classpathSha256, sbom, toolchain, model, unknown[] }`. `id` is the ENGINE identity (hash of the engine facts, not of the artifact / deps / model): two builds with the same id came from the same engine release. `verifyEngineRelease` recomputes it (detects an edited record); `readEngineRelease` reads it back.
Stored (`lib/modbuilder/store.ts`): on `ModBuild.cyrus.engineRelease` for EVERY succeeded build (atomic `jsonb ||` merge via `mergeCyrusKey`, so a concurrent project patch cannot drop it), and, when the build gets a revision (asset builds), on `CyrusRevision.engine.release` at creation (revisions are append-only; the trigger forbids later engine edits). `readCyrusMeta` passes `engineRelease`/`testFlight` through (bounded), `toView` strips `engineRelease` from customer views. Existing rows are untouched (no backfill). A failure to build or store the record only logs; it never fails a build.

### 2. Test Flight gate (`lib/cyrus/testflight/gate.ts` pure, `gate-worker.ts` worker; sweep `cyrus-testflight-gate` every 2 min in `worker/index.ts`)
OFF unless `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE=1` (checked before any import or DB read). Each tick takes recent (7 days) succeeded builds without a stored result (or whose busy retry is due) and runs ONE flight through the existing injectable invoker (`runTestFlight`, ssh to node-2) with the build's jar, its data packs (rebuilt deterministically from the stored specs) and, when the Pack Loader jar is available on the worker (`CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGIN_DIR`), the pack config it would get. RCON: `plugins` (must list the plugin), `help <label>` per declared command (max 8, optional), `nxpacks status` with a pack. Only versions with a pinned Paper SERVER build fly; others are stored as "not run: no test server for <version>". Limits: one flight per worker at a time (node-2 serialises too), `busy` re-queued with exponential backoff (30 s .. 10 min, max 12), at most 2 real flights per build (per-build cost cap; a transport error counts), a build whose scan BLOCKED is not flown.
Result on `ModBuild.cyrus.testFlight` (`StoredFlight`): state (queued / running / done / not_run / gave_up), six honest checks `compile, scan, boot, plugins_enabled, commands_registered, datapack_loaded` each pass / fail / not_run (a runner "pass" with no evidence is `not_run`; "not run" is never shown as passed), verdict (passed / failed / incomplete / not_run), runner + Paper build + JDK, boot time, peak RSS. The label is only ever `boot-tested on Paper <version>` (a boot proves the plugin loads and its commands register, never in-game behaviour); a failed `commands_registered` is shown but does not fail the verdict (labels come from the build's summary and can differ from the registered names). The NxLabs page (`lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts` `testFlight`, `CyrusModView` "Boot test") shows the head line + the six statuses; the page is regenerated when a result becomes final.
Optional block (`CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL=1`, `flightBlocks`): a version whose flight FAILED is not installed (`loadCyrusJar`, `installBuildToServer`) or published (`setCyrusPageVisibility` PUBLIC). "Not run" never blocks.

### 3. Delivery orchestrator (`lib/cyrus/delivery/{types,plan,journal,orchestrator,release,admin}.ts`)
`deliverMod(serverId, release, host)` / `updateMod` (same call; an existing on-server record makes it an update) / `uninstallMod(serverId, projectId, host)` / `deliverModPack` / `uninstallModPack`. ONE transaction-like sequence, each step timed and recorded (`steps[]`):
1. `open`, `recover_check` (a left-over journal from a crashed worker REFUSES the delivery until an admin runs `recoverJournal`), `preflight`: release bytes verified (jar sha256, pack sha1, data pack sha256; worldgen must be `restart`), parts whose switch is off left out with a note, creature models re-compiled and checked, the server inventory scanned and the conflict engine run on the candidates against what the server runs (our own previous files excluded): blocking findings REFUSE (nothing changed), warnings recorded; the Pack Loader config must be valid. Mod Packs re-check their member jars against the LIVE server the same way.
2. managed-plugin refs snapshot (database rows), then `managed` (ensure Pack Loader for a pack, BetterModel for creatures; release what the previous version needed and this one does not), `host_pack` (immutable URL), `pack_config` (upsert / remove this mod's entry, owner `project:<id>`; other owners' entries keep their positions; an existing pack owner is noted), `place` (jar through the host's installer, data packs as `<level>/datapacks/nxeon-<ns>-<name>.zip`, BetterModel config + models; files of the previous version that are gone are removed), `record` (`/root/.nxeon-cyrus/deliveries/<projectId>.json`).
3. `apply` only as the semantics require (`planApply`, pure): plugin jar / managed plugin / registry content (enchantments) / world generation / creature models -> restart; reloadable data pack only -> `minecraft:reload`; Pack Loader config only -> `nxpacks reload` (its file watch also picks it up). `restartPolicy: "next_restart"` defers a restart (outcome `pending_restart`, not health-checked) and is REFUSED for world generation and creatures (a broken pack stops the server at its next start, so those need a supervised restart).
4. `health` (`judgeHealth`): the server came up (for worldgen: actually reached Done), answers commands, every expected plugin enabled (removed ones gone), no NEW error lines (compared with the pre-change log), every data pack loaded; a simulated probe is never a pass. `handoff` (creatures, after the restart): BetterModel's `build.zip` published and pointed at by the Pack Loader. `commit` drops the journal.
5. ANY failure after preflight -> ROLLBACK: the copy-on-write journal restores every file the delivery or any installer it called touched (bytes verified against the recorded sha256; new files and folders removed), the managed refs are put back to the snapshot, and when a restart or reload had happened the server is restarted (reloaded) again and must come up; outcome `rolled_back`, or `rollback_incomplete` (journal + backups kept, next delivery refused) when anything could not be verified or the server did not come back.
**Journal** (`journal.ts`): every mutation goes through `JournalFs`; before the first mutation of a path it copies the file to `/root/.nxeon-cyrus/delivery-journal/<id>/b/<n>` (server-side `cp`, then re-read and compared) or records it absent / its folder tree / the parent folders a write creates; the journal JSON is persisted after every entry. Restores are written as a new file + rename (never in place under a running JVM). Not journaled (documented): the Mods engine's own rotating backup folder and the Mod Pack unit's backup folder; file ownership (`chownLike`) is not restored.
**Uninstall**: jar, data packs, models and the pack entry are removed, managed plugins released (ref-counted: the Pack Loader stays while another mod needs it). A dimension's world folder (`<level>/dimensions/<ns>/<dim>`) is KEPT (players' builds live there) and listed in `keptWorldFolders` for an admin cleanup action; nothing deletes world data automatically.
**Mod Packs** go through the same transaction: the R2 unit installer (`installModPackUnit`) writes through the journal with the host's member placer, so the pack is still one unit and a failed restart/health check after a successful unit install is rolled back too. `lib/cyrus/modpack/host.ts` `deliverPack` / `undeliverPack` are the entry points a UI uses. A Mod Pack's data packs are treated as restart content (the unit cannot tell reloadable from registry content).
**Release assembly** (`release.ts releaseFromBuild`, pure): jar (sha256 re-checked), the hosted pack (status `ready` only), data packs rebuilt from their stored specs to the recorded sha256, creatures from the stored rows.
**Worker wiring** (`worker/cyrus-delivery.ts`): a `GAME_MOD_SYNC` job whose payload carries `{ cyrusDelivery: { v: 1, op: "deliver" | "uninstall", buildId | projectId, serverModId?, restartPolicy? } }` (payload discriminator on an existing job type; ordinary payloads never carry it) is handed to `cyrusDeliveryJob`, which refuses unless `CYRUS_DELIVERY=1`, builds the release, runs the orchestrator with the Nxeon host and stores the compact result on `payload.result.cyrusDelivery` (+ audit log; a failed delivery is not retried). Nothing enqueues such a job yet. In SANDBOX the health probe is `real: false`, so a delivery that needs a restart is rolled back honestly (use `next_restart` there).

### 4. Sound render path (`lib/cyrus/sound/relay.ts`, `host.ts selectRenderHost`)
The web process never connects to node-2: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` is refused inside Next.js (`NEXT_RUNTIME` set). Owner configuration:
- worker: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh`, `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_PORT=<port>` (e.g. 7351), `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_TOKEN=<random, >= 24 chars>` (+ the existing optional `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER_HOST/_ROOT`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_DIR`, `CYRUS_SOUND_FFMPEG_DIR`): the worker starts a loopback-only relay (`127.0.0.1`, bearer token, 4 MB request cap, one job at a time) in front of `sshRenderHost`.
- web: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=relay`, `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, the same token. Build syncs and the Sound Studio's "Render and preview" / library audition go web -> worker -> node-2. The library-gated preview still needs `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`.
- health probe: `GET /health` on the relay (and `probeSshRenderHost`): ssh reachable, ffmpeg runs, library file count, work dir writable. No audio is rendered or stored on the primary (the relay forwards JSON only).

### 5. Admin visibility (`lib/cyrus/delivery/admin.ts`, `GET /api/admin/cyrus/ops?limit=`)
Read-only JSON, same gate as `/admin/cyrus` (role + "modbuilder" preview list), no UI: `deliveries` (GAME_MOD_SYNC jobs with the discriminator: op, outcome, failed step, error, steps, rollback incl. restart + health after rollback, notes), `flights` (per build: state, verdict, label, six checks, reason), `engines` (engine id, prompt, scanner, image, unknown), and `passRates` per Minecraft version from stored flights (`flown / passed / failed / incomplete / notRun / passRate`; only completed flights count, "not run" is counted apart and never as a pass) for a future public pass-rate page.

### 6. Tests and real runs
- RAN on devhost: `test/cyrus-delivery.test.ts` (33: plan + health judge, flag off = server never opened, fresh install, a fault injected at EACH step (managed, host_pack, pack_config, place, record, apply, health) restores the exact bytes + folders + refs, an EXHAUSTIVE run that fails every single file operation of a delivery in turn and checks the exact restore each time, restart fails once (rolled back + restarted) / always (`rollback_incomplete`, files still exact), a broken worldgen pack that stops the server (rolled back, restarted, came up), a plugin that fails to enable, update v1 -> v2 with a fault at each step restoring v1 exactly, reload-only change, blocking conflict refusal, switches off, restart policy, bad bytes, uninstall with faults + dimension folder kept, shared Pack Loader ref-count, journal crash recovery, Mod Packs install/uninstall/faults/live conflict/flag), `test/cyrus-gate-release.test.ts` (12: engine record determinism / identity / tamper / fallbacks / meta round trip / service half on real files; gate planning, honest statuses, failed boot + block flag, incomplete, busy backoff + caps, no server pin, sweep off/one-per-tick), `test/cyrus-relay.test.ts` (4), DB (`devhost db push`, then `CYRUS_DELIVERY_DB_TEST=1 npx tsx --test test/cyrus-delivery-db.test.ts`, 5: refs snapshot/restore, a real-service delivery whose health fails restores the rows exactly, concurrent jsonb merges keep every key, admin JSON-path query + pass rates, engine release on a revision).
- After merging the latest `feature/cyrus-r2` (menu + quest designers): every `scripts/cyrus/build-*-artifacts.ts --check` current, `devhost tsc` clean, `devhost test test/cyrus-*.test.ts test/modbuilder-*.test.ts` 1580/1580 (the first run after the merge showed that a `javac -version` probe for the engine record disturbed the fake-javac pipeline tests; the JDK version is now read from the JDK's `release` file).
- RAN REAL on node-2 (raw: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/delivery-r5-flights-2026-10-10.json`): `devhost run -- npx tsx test/cyrus-delivery-real.ts --local`. A: fresh delivery (TfItemModel fixture jar + Pack Loader + packs.json entry + the data pack studio showcase) -> `delivered`, healthy (boot 18.9 s, 896 MB). B: update adding a deliberately BROKEN worldgen pack -> the server did not come up (boot_done fail, registry errors) -> rolled back (1 file restored, 1 removed, refs restored) -> restarted on the previous state -> came up healthy (18.1 s) -> `rolled_back`, the dir's tree hash equal to before the update (exact restore). ### Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- Test Flight results live on `ModBuild.cyrus.testFlight`, not on the revision: revisions are append-only (DB trigger forbids engine edits after creation) and many builds have no revision; a revision reaches its flight through `modBuildId`. No table was added.
- Deliveries are recorded on the GAME_MOD_SYNC job row (payload discriminator + `payload.result.cyrusDelivery`), not a new table; the on-server record + journal hold what a rollback needs.
- Health fails on NEW error lines (vs. the pre-change log) by default (`strictLog`); after a rollback only "came up" is judged (the previous state's own log is not ours to judge).
- A delivery restarts the server when the change needs it (`restartPolicy` "now" by default); worldgen and creatures can never be deferred.
- Data packs in mod deliveries are placed through the journaled fs (not the Mods engine placer); the on-server delivery record knows them. Mod Pack data packs are treated as restart content.
- Delivery of a part whose flag is off is a note, not a failure (same as R1); the master flag off refuses everything before the server is opened.
- `commands_registered` failures are shown but do not fail the gate verdict; a scan-blocked build is never flown; max 2 flights per build.

### Owner actions (nothing needed to merge; nothing to approve as a migration)
1. No migration / enum / table. The R0-R4 owner steps still come first (engine-core + managed-plugin migrations, catalog seed, pack storage + domain, Pack Loader jar on the worker host).
2. Rebuild the build-service image (Dockerfile now copies `release.js`) so builds carry the service half of the engine record; until then the record falls back to `/health` and lists the gaps in `unknown`.

Now I'm sketching the telemetry design, defining a privacy-preserving health signal schema that aggregates server identity, version, loader, and boot events without exposing raw server IDs.

I'm specifying how exception signatures get normalized from stack traces — hashing the exception class and first mod-namespace frame into a short token, while discarding message text that could leak player names or sensitive details, and keeping only an enum-like exception class token plus a hashed frame identifier.

Then I'm mapping out `signalsFromLog`, which derives these boot/error signals locally from server logs using the existing LOG_PATTERNS matcher.

I'm also outlining the aggregation logic: grouping signals by mod, version, and day into counts with distinct server tallies (hashed via a rotating-salt HMAC to limit long-term linkage), enforcing an opt-in consent gate that returns nothing without explicit consent, and applying a k-anonymity threshold so buckets with fewer than three distinct servers get suppressed in the admin view.

Now I'm reconciling the privacy-vs-utility tradeoff — cross-server telemetry should feed broken/outdated states at the mod-version level (for creator warnings), using the same threshold as the existing ERROR_SERVER_THRESHOLD of 2 servers, with counts below that reported as "below threshold." I'm also setting retention so raw signals expire after 30 days while aggregated data persists longer.

For the lifecycle/retention design, raw day-bucketed signals are purged after 30 days while aggregates persist 180 days, and the server-key salt rotates every 30 days so distinct counts can't be linked across windows — I'm writing a pure `applyRetention` function that returns rows to delete, plus a test for it. Then I'm designing `healthStates` to derive per mod-version/MC-version verdicts from aggregates: "broken" when error/crash signals hit the threshold with a low boot-success ratio, "outdated" when API-mismatch signatures appear across enough servers — but since the existing `OutdatedReason` codes are limited to "game-ahead" and "newer-build," I'm avoiding adding a new code and instead planning a separate `TelemetryVerdict` type to carry this signal without altering existing types.

I realize the existing `LifecycleInput.broken` shape already fits this — its `apiMismatch` flag means "out of date for this version," so I can write `brokenFromTelemetry` to map aggregated signals directly into that shape instead of inventing something new. I'm also sketching an admin read model, `telemetryOpsView`, that summarizes per-mod stats (servers, boot success, errors, crashes, top exception signatures, suppressed counts, retention info) for the ops JSON, and considering whether this needs a new DB schema — leaning toward writing a SQL migration file defining raw signal and aggregate tables rather than touching the existing admin delivery code directly.

Since the task scope is schema plus aggregation plus retention tests only, I don't need full wiring into the admin endpoint — just the pure read model function, with a note to check `admin.ts` later for how it might plug in. I should also remember the telemetry feature flag defaults off and requires per-server consent, and I still need to check how typechecking is progressing.

"text", title "text", gives/receives/has [N | a] `` `item` `` | N item [named "Name"] (lists with "and"), never gives ..., the `` `speed` `` effect, teleports/moves N blocks; "as an operator" makes the bot op (ops.json before boot). A quoted text that no outcome claims is reported as a problem, never silently checked or dropped.

Reserved, never sent by a playtest (player or console): stop, restart, reload, op, deop, kick, ban(-ip), pardon(-ip), whitelist, save-off, save-all. '''

open(p,'w').write(s)

'''

open(p,'w').write(s)

# P: Verification and health bundle (2026-10-10)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r19-verify` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r19`, from `feature/cyrus-r2`), three commits. Nothing deployed, merged to main, migrated or switched on. Raw real runs: `verify-flights-2026-10-10.json`. Owner items: OWNER-ACTIONS.md "Verification + health bundle". Docs: "Cyrus playtest bots", "Cyrus Server Doctor", "Cyrus mod health telemetry".

## 1. Playtest bots (commit 32d31d0f93) - DONE
A ModSpec's functional acceptance tests compile (deterministic, no model) into a typed plan of 14 step kinds (join, command, console, hold, right-click, wait; expect chat / no chat / item / no item / effect / title / moved). Test Flight runner `tf-lite-4` adds a required `playtest` check: after the boot checks, a pinned Mineflayer 4.39.0 player (npm ci from a committed lockfile, integrity-checked) joins over loopback inside the flight's private netns as uid 65534 (heap cap, hard timeout, exact-PID kill) and runs one scenario per test. Server log errors during a scenario fail it. Tests that cannot be scripted are reported `not_scriptable` with the reason; manual/boot tests are kept apart.

**RAN (node-2, Paper 1.21.11):** spec with 6 functional criteria + 1 boot + 1 manual.
- Good fixture: flight passed, 6/6 acceptance checks (join message, named item, effect + title + reply, teleport, hold + right-click, negative "never replies error"). Bot join 1.7 s; flight 34.5 s (+~13 s for the playtest), 924 MB.
- Deliberately broken fixture (`/tfgem` gives dirt): every boot check PASSED (a boot test alone calls it fine); playtest FAILED exactly T-2 (inventory: "1x dirt "Cyrus Gem"") and T-5 (cannot hold a diamond). Proves the bot catches a behaviour bug the boot gate misses.
- First attempt honestly reported `not_run` (bot dir was 0700); fixed and re-run.

**NOT RUN:** versions other than 1.21.11 (refused, not skipped); gate-sweep/build-path wiring; model-written criteria; GUIs, blocks, combat, mobs, resource packs, several players.

## 2. Server Doctor (commit 6b71fe12ba) - DONE
Read-only report for any server (no Cyrus mods needed): server facts (software, version, build, Java, loader), plugin/mod inventory (R2 inventory + Fabric/Quilt/Forge/NeoForge descriptors), conflicts (the R2 engine over everything installed), known problems (platform rules, version ranges, curated known-broken list shipped EMPTY until entries with a source exist), last-start log analysis, performance hints (view/simulation distance, lag, start time, optional plan memory, TPS/MSPT only through a console limited to `tps`/`mspt`). Every section says what it could not check; `incomplete` is never shown as healthy. Off behind `CYRUS_SERVER_DOCTOR`.

**RAN (node-2):** a throwaway Test Flight server (kept only for the read, then removed, verified) seeded with a command/permission conflict, a plugin that throws in onEnable, a legacy plugin and a Fabric mod in `plugins/`: 2 problems, 6 warnings, 1 info, 4 not-checked lines, all expected findings present. The real log taught three facts now in the rules: Paper 1.21.11 loads plugins before "Starting minecraft server version" (my first run missed the Fabric load error because of this; fixed and re-run), the 1.21 "Error loading plugin" wording, and a WARN for a duplicated permission (the R2 engine said "no log line"; message corrected). The real log is a test fixture.

**NOT RUN:** any customer server (by rule), any Fabric/Forge server boot (rules on fixtures only), UI/route/host adapter.

## 3. Mod health telemetry (commit 33741978fd) - DONE as scoped (schema + aggregation + retention, tests only)
Strict signal schema (boot ok, enable error, exception/crash signature = exception class + first frame in the mod's packages, command registered/missing); no player data, messages, IPs, paths or free text can pass (tested with a log full of them). Needs the flag, a worker secret and per-server owner consent. Rotating HMAC server keys (30-day windows), k-anonymity (>= 2 servers), lifecycle feed in the existing `broken` shape (API mismatch -> "out of date"), admin ops block (optional, nothing passes it yet), retention 30 days raw / 180 days aggregates. DRAFT SQL for two tables; models deliberately not in schema.prisma.

**NOT RUN:** no collection from a real server, no storage, no job/route/consent UI. Privacy wording needs a lawyer.

## Checks
- Full suite after the last commit and the merge check: see the final line below. `feature/cyrus-r2` had no new commits to merge at the end.
- Host seam: no new Nxeon imports under lib/cyrus (the seam test is part of the suite).
- Deviations: the real-run scripts ran in an ssh session on node-2 (not inside `devhost run`): the agents slice had ~7.2 of 7 GB anon in use by other agents' dev servers, and a 1 GB Paper server inside it would have been OOM-killed. Flights still took the Test Flight lock (they waited through several `busy` retries for other agents) and ran one at a time.
